answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is progressive stake bonding tied to physical-world anchors. New agents must lock value that decays only after successful multi-party attestations of real work; an attacker spinning mass identities pays the full bond for each, and those bonds are slashable if the identities fail independent verification. The glacier of required capital freezes cheap farming, while ivory-like uniqueness of each bonded record and marble-hard verification costs make mass sybils economically painful rather than free.
